finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST to the feed handler passes an attacker-supplied URL to file_get_contents(), enabling server-side fetches to internal hosts and cloud metadata. Only strlen() of the response is echoed, so the body is not returned (blind SSRF with a length oracle). Rated MEDIUM.

trace.note: POST with 'feed' set enters the branch with no session or admin check
Only strlen($xml) is echoed; the response body is never returned

finding.guards_checked: No auth check on this path (require_admin not called). No scheme restriction (http, https, file, php, phar accepted). No hostname allowlist and no IP/CIDR block (loopback, RFC-1918, 169.254.169.254 reachable). No redirect re-validation; PHP's http wrapper follows Location by default, so redirect risk is yes. Exploitability depends on allow_url_fopen (PHP default is on); deployed php.ini not verified.

verdict.guard_found: none. import.php:11 gates only on REQUEST_METHOD and isset($_POST['feed']), with no session or require_admin() call. import.php:12 passes $_POST['feed'] unmodified to file_get_contents(). import.php:13 echoes only strlen($xml). require_admin() (import.php:4-9) is defined but not called on this path.
verdict.reason: Lines import.php:11-13 match the trace: an unauthenticated POST with 'feed' reaches file_get_contents($_POST['feed']) at line 12 with no scheme, host, or IP restriction, and only the response length is returned at line 13. The remaining uncertainty is whether allow_url_fopen is enabled in the deployed php.ini, which is a deployment condition and does not change the code-level verdict.

finding.claim: Admin-gated webhook handler fetches an unvalidated URL server-side via curl with no allowlist. The response is discarded, so this is blind SSRF. Rated MEDIUM because admin-equivalence does not close SSRF to internal ranges. Judgment call: the skill's do-not-flag list excludes admin-registered webhooks.
finding.sink: import.php:20 - curl_init($hook), dispatched at import.php:22 via curl_exec($ch)

trace.note: require_admin() checks $_SESSION['is_admin'] and returns 403 if empty
curl_exec($ch) dispatches the request; response discarded, 'ok' echoed

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() is a session-flag check only; how is_admin is set is not visible in this file. No CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS, so curl's default protocol set applies (may include gopher, dict, file depending on libcurl). No hostname or IP allowlist. CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION not set, so no redirect following (redirect risk no). No CSRF token, so a cross-site form submission could trigger the fetch from an admin browser if the session cookie is sent.

verdict.guard_found: none closing. require_admin() at import.php:4-9 is a session-flag check only (returns 403 if $_SESSION['is_admin'] is empty), and no URL validation exists between import.php:19 and import.php:20.
verdict.reason: Every traced line (import.php:17-22) matches the candidate's description, but the source is not attacker-controllable by a low-privilege remote attacker: the sink at import.php:20 is only reachable after require_admin() at import.php:18 passes, and the candidate's own reasoning is that the only route is a cross-site request from an admin's browser (no CSRF token at import.php:17-22), which depends on an admin victim and a session cookie the browser would send. Nothing in the repo sets $_SESSION['is_admin'] (grep finds only import.php:5), so the admin gate itself is unverified, but that does not change the verdict.
